stories.text: A prince wanted to marry a real princess. He looked in every castle for a princess. But he never found anyone. One night, a storm came to the castle. Someone knocked at the castle gate in the rain. A girl stood outside in the storm. "I am a real princess," the girl said. The queen put a pea under twenty beds. That night, the girl lay on all the beds. She felt a hard pea under her all night. "I did not sleep at all," the princess said. So the prince married the real princess the next day.

stories.text: A fisherman lived in a small hut by the sea with his wife. One day he caught a golden fish that asked to be set free. "Let me go, and I will grant you a wish," said the fish. He let it go and went home with nothing at all. His wife was angry and sent him back to ask for a cottage instead of the hut. The fish granted it, and the wife was happy for a while. Soon she wanted a big house, then a castle, then to be king. Each time the fisherman went back to the sea, and each time the fish granted the wish. The sea grew darker and rougher with every wish. Then she wanted to be emperor, and after that pope. At last she wanted to be like God. The fisherman went to the sea in a storm and told the fish. This time the fish said nothing and swam away. When the fisherman came home, the castle was gone and they were back in the little hut.

q.en: Is the wife greedy, or is she right to want more?

model.en: Wanting a better house is fair; a hut by the sea is a hard place to live. The problem is that no size ever satisfies her: cottage, house, castle, king, emperor, pope, and then God. She stops asking for comfort and starts asking for rank, and that is where the story turns.
model.fa: خواستن خانهٔ بهتر منصفانه است؛ کلبه‌ای کنار دریا جای سختی برای زندگی است. مشکل این است که هیچ اندازه‌ای راضی‌اش نمی‌کند: خانه، عمارت، قلعه، پادشاه، امپراتور، پاپ و بعد خدا. دیگر آسایش نمی‌خواهد و مقام می‌خواهد، و داستان همان‌جا می‌چرخد.

tip.en: Find the exact point where the wish stops being reasonable.
tip.fa: دقیقاً همان جایی را پیدا کن که آرزو دیگر معقول نیست.

model.en: The sea is the one thing that cannot be granted. It starts calm and ends in a storm, so the reader can see the size of each wish without being told. The fish says nothing, but the water answers.
model.fa: دریا تنها چیزی است که نمی‌شود برآورد. آرام شروع می‌شود و به طوفان می‌رسد، تا خواننده بی‌آنکه به او گفته شود بزرگی هر آرزو را ببیند. ماهی چیزی نمی‌گوید، اما آب پاسخ می‌دهد.

tip.fa: یک جزئیات را که حس را حمل می‌کند انتخاب کن و توضیحش بده.

pairs.fa: امپراتوری لباس تازه را بیشتر از هر چیز دیگری در دنیا دوست داشت.

pairs.en: Two strangers came to the city and said they could weave a wonderful cloth.
pairs.fa: دو غریبه به شهر آمدند و گفتند می‌توانند پارچهٔ شگفت‌انگیزی ببافند.

pairs.en: The cloth, they said, was invisible to anyone stupid or bad at their job.
pairs.fa: به گفتهٔ آن‌ها پارچه برای هر احمق یا هر کس که کارش را بد انجام دهد نامرئی بود.

pairs.en: The emperor paid them a lot of gold and told them to begin at once.
pairs.fa: امپراتور پول زیادی به آن‌ها داد و گفت بی‌درنگ شروع کنند.

pairs.en: They put up an empty loom and worked all day, moving their hands over nothing.
pairs.fa: دستگاهی خالی برپا کردند و تمام روز کار کردند و دست‌هایشان را روی هیچ حرکت می‌دادند.

pairs.fa: امپراتور اول وزیر سالخورده‌ای را فرستاد پارچه را ببیند.

pairs.en: The minister saw nothing, but he did not want to look stupid, so he said it was beautiful.

pairs.en: Another man was sent, and he told the same lie.

pairs.en: At last the emperor went himself, and he saw nothing at all.
pairs.fa: سرانجام خود امپراتور رفت و هیچ چیز ندید.

pairs.en: "How beautiful!" he said, because he could not admit that he saw nothing.

pairs.en: The strangers helped him put on the new clothes, and he walked through the streets.

stories.text: An emperor loved new clothes more than anything else in the world. Two strangers came to the city and said they could weave a wonderful cloth. The cloth, they said, was invisible to anyone stupid or bad at their job. The emperor paid them a lot of gold and told them to begin at once. They put up an empty loom and worked all day, moving their hands over nothing. The emperor sent an old minister to look at the cloth first. The minister saw nothing, but he did not want to look stupid, so he said it was beautiful. Another man was sent, and he told the same lie. At last the emperor went himself, and he saw nothing at all. "How beautiful!" he said, because he could not admit that he saw nothing. The strangers helped him put on the new clothes, and he walked through the streets. Everybody in the street shouted how beautiful the clothes were. Then a little child said, "But he has nothing on!" People began to repeat it, and the emperor knew it was true, but he walked on.

stories.text: A miller told the king that his daughter could spin straw into gold. The king called the girl to the castle and locked her in a room full of straw. "Spin this into gold by morning," he said, "or you must die." The girl did not know what to do, so she sat down and cried. A little man came in through the window and asked what she would give him. She gave him her necklace, and by morning all the straw was gold. The king wanted more, so he gave her a bigger room and the same promise. She had nothing left, so she promised her first child, and the little man spun the straw. The king married her, and a year later she had a baby. The little man came for the child, and she begged him to leave it. He said she could keep it if she guessed his name in three days. She sent messengers all over the country to collect every name they heard. On the second night a messenger heard a little man singing by a fire. "Rumpelstiltskin is my name," the song said. The queen said the name, and the little man stamped his foot and tore himself in two.

stories.text: An old woman baked a gingerbread man in her small kitchen. She shaped the dough into a little man, gave him eyes and a smile, and put him in the oven. When she opened the oven door, he jumped out and ran out of the house. "Run, run, as fast as you can! You can't catch me, I'm the Gingerbread Man!" The old woman and the old man chased him, but they were slow and soon out of breath. A cow in a field called, "Stop! I want to eat you!" He did not stop; he called back that he had already run from two people. A horse by a barn could not catch him either, so he ran on alone. Then he came to a wide river that was too deep to cross. He could not swim, and water would make him soft and ruin him. A fox came out of the woods and asked why he was standing there. "I can carry you across," said the fox. "I only want to help." "You will not eat me?" asked the Gingerbread Man. He climbed onto the fox's back, then onto his head, then onto his nose as the water rose. The fox opened his mouth wide and ate him in one bite. The chase was over, and the fox was not hungry any more.

stories.text: Henny Penny lived on a farm and often stood under a big tree. One day an acorn fell from the tree and hit her on the head. She did not see it fall, so she was sure something terrible had happened. "The sky is falling!" she cried. "I must tell the king!" She ran off the farm and down a road, and soon she met a rooster. His name was Cocky Locky, and he asked her where she was going. "The sky is falling," she said. "I will come with you," he answered. By a pond they met Ducky Lucky, and by a field they met Goosey Loosey. At a barn Turkey Lurkey joined them, so five birds walked on together. The road led into the woods, where Foxy Loxy came out to meet them. "I know a short way to the king," said the fox. "Follow me." The short way led to his den, but the birds did not know that. "Only one bird can go in at a time," said the fox at the den. Cocky Locky went in and did not come out; Ducky Lucky went in and did not come out. Goosey Loosey and Turkey Lurkey went in too, and neither came out. Henny Penny heard a noise inside, and it scared her, so she did not go in. She ran all the way home, and she never told the king about the sky.

model.en: Foxy Loxy does the harm, but the rumour starts it. Henny Penny never checks what hit her, and each bird repeats her words without asking a question, so five birds follow a stranger into a den. The fox only has to offer a short way.

stories.text: A princess lived in a big castle with her father, the king. She had a little ball of gold, and she loved to play with it. One day she played by an old well that was deep and full of water. She threw the ball up high, but it fell into the well. The ball went down and did not come back, so the princess cried. Then a green frog came up out of the well and asked why she was crying. "I can get your ball," said the frog, "but you must be my friend." "Let me eat with you and live with you," he said. "Yes, yes! I promise!" the princess said. The frog went down and came back up with the gold ball. The princess took the ball and ran to the castle, and she forgot the frog. The next day, at dinner, they heard a tap at the door. The frog sat on the step and said, "You made a promise to me." The king said, "A princess must keep her promise. Open the door." So the frog came in and ate from the gold plate, but the princess did not like it. Later the frog asked to sleep in her room, and the king told her to take him up. The frog was kind, and soon she was not afraid and gave him a kiss. The frog became a young prince: a witch had put a spell on him. They were married in the castle and lived happily for many years.

stories.text: A little red hen lived in a small farmyard. She lived there with her chicks. The chicks were too small to work. A cat, a dog, and a pig lived nearby. The hen wanted fresh bread for her hungry chicks. One day, she found wheat seeds on the ground. "Who will help me plant the wheat?" she asked. "Not I," said the cat. "Not I," said the dog. "Not I," said the pig. "Then I will plant it myself," said the hen. So she planted the wheat in a small field. Sun and rain fell on the small field every day. The hen pulled the weeds herself. The wheat grew tall in the sun. Soon the wheat turned a golden color. The hen looked at the tall wheat. "The wheat is ready to cut," she said. "Who will help me cut the wheat?" she asked. "Not I," said the dog. "Not I," said the pig. "Not I," said the cat. "Then I will cut it myself," she said. The hen cut the wheat alone. The cut wheat lay in a big pile. The hen wanted to grind it into flour. "Who will help me grind the wheat?" she asked. She looked at the cat, dog, and pig. "Not I," they all said. "Then I will grind it myself," said the hen. The hen had to grind the wheat alone. Soon the wheat became white flour. The hen put the flour into a bag. The hen mixed the flour with water. She made a soft dough. "Who will help me bake the bread?" she asked. "Not I," said the pig. "Not I," said the cat. "Not I," said the dog. "Then I will bake it myself," she said. The hen had to bake the bread alone. She put the dough into a hot oven. Soon a warm smell filled the small house. The cat, dog, and pig smelled it from far away. The cat, dog, and pig came to the house. "That smells so good," said the cat. "Who will eat this bread?" asked the hen. "Give it to me!" said the cat. "I want some too!" said the dog. "Share it with us!" said the pig. "You did not help me," said the hen. "My chicks and I will eat it," she said. So the hen ate the warm bread with her chicks. The bread tasted sweet. The chicks pecked every crumb from the plate. The cat, dog, and pig walked away hungry.

stories.text: A poor shoemaker had only one piece of leather. He lived with his wife in a small shop. That evening, he cut the leather into shapes for shoes. He left the pieces on the table. The shoemaker went to bed. In the morning, he came back to the shop. Two perfect shoes stood on the table. Soon a rich man came into the shop. He tried on the shoes and loved them. He paid the shoemaker a lot of gold for them. The shoemaker bought leather for two pairs of shoes. That night, he cut the leather into shapes again. He left the pieces on the table. In the morning, two pairs of shoes stood there. Two more customers came and bought them. Soon the shoemaker had gold for leather for four pairs. Every night, he cut leather for more shoes. Every morning, shoes stood on the table. People came from other towns to buy his shoes. The shoemaker and his wife became rich from the shoes. But the shoemaker never saw who made the shoes. He wanted to know who helped him every night. "Let us hide and know who helps us," he said. That night, he cut leather again. He left the pieces on the table. Then the shoemaker and his wife hid. They waited quietly for midnight. At midnight, two little elves ran into the shop. The elves had no clothes on. They climbed on the table. The elves cut and sewed the leather into shoes. Before the sun came up, the elves ran out. "We must thank the two little elves," said the wife. "They have no clothes, even in the cold," she said. She took cloth and sewed tiny shirts and coats. The shoemaker cut leather for two shoes to match. That night, they put the clothes on the table. They put the tiny shoes with the clothes. This time, they left no leather on the table. Then the shoemaker and his wife hid and watched again. They waited quietly for the elves to come. At midnight, the two elves ran into the shop. But no leather was on the table. They saw tiny shirts, coats, and shoes. The shoemaker and his wife watched. The elves put on the shirts and the coats. They put the shoes on. The two elves laughed and danced around the room. They danced out the door. The elves ran out and never came back. The shoemaker did not need help again. He stayed rich and lived for many years.

stories.text: Three little pigs lived with their mother. They lived in a small home in the woods. One day, their mother called the three pigs. "You are big pigs now," she said. "Go and build houses of your own," she said. "But watch out for the wolf!" she called. A wolf lived deep in the woods. The wolf liked to eat little pigs. The three pigs said goodbye to their mother. They left home to build their own houses. Each pig went a different way. The first pig found a pile of straw. He built a house of straw in one day. "Now I can play all day," he said. The second pig found sticks in the woods. He built a house of sticks in two days. The stick house was stronger than the straw house. The third pig remembered the wolf. He wanted a strong house, so he gathered many bricks. The bricks were heavy and slow to carry. The brick house took many days to build. But the third pig was tired and did not stop. At last, the brick house was done. Soon, the wolf was hungry. He went to find the three pigs. The wolf found the house of straw. He knocked on the door. "Little pig, let me come in!" called the wolf. "No, I won't let you in!" said the first pig. "I'll huff and puff and blow your house down!" The wolf huffed. The wolf puffed. The straw house fell down. The first pig ran to the second pig's house. He was safe inside the stick house. The wolf was still hungry. He went to find the pigs. Soon, the wolf found the stick house. Two little pigs were inside. "Little pigs, let me come in!" called the wolf. "No, we won't let you in!" said the pigs. "I'll huff and puff and blow your house down!" The wolf huffed and puffed hard. This time, the house did not fall fast. But the stick house fell down too. Both pigs ran to the third pig's house. They were safe inside the brick house. All three pigs were inside the brick house. The wolf found them. "Little pigs, let me come in!" called the wolf. "No, we won't let you in!" said the pigs. "I'll huff and puff and blow your house down!" The wolf huffed and puffed hard. But the brick house did not move. The wolf huffed and puffed. Still, the house did not fall. The wolf stopped to rest. He wanted another way into the house. The wolf saw the chimney on the roof. The wolf climbed up onto the roof. The third pig heard him up there. "He will come down the chimney," said the third pig. The third pig heated a pot of water. Soon, the water in the pot was hot. The wolf climbed down the dark chimney. Splash! The wolf fell into the hot water. He jumped out with a yelp. The wolf ran out through the door. He ran into the woods and never came back. Now the three pigs were safe forever.

q.en: Was the first pig lazy or just in a hurry?

model.en: The story says he wanted to play all day, so lazy is fairer than hurried. He chose the fastest house because he wanted the afternoon free, and that choice is exactly what the wolf punished.

stories.text: Three goats lived on a bare hill. Little Goat, Middle Goat, and Big Goat were hungry. The grass on their hill was thin and dry. Across the bridge, a green hill stood tall. Middle Goat: Look at that fresh grass! Big Goat: We will go across the bridge. Little Goat: I will go first. Middle Goat: Good. We will wait here. Little Goat walked down to the bridge. Under the bridge, a troll lived in the dark. Little Goat's hooves went trip-trap on the bridge. Troll: Who is trip-trapping over my bridge? Little Goat: It is only me, the little goat. Troll: I will eat you up! Little Goat: Do not eat me, Troll. Little Goat: Wait for my brother, Middle Goat. Little Goat: He is bigger than me. Troll: Bigger, you say? Troll: Then go, little goat. Little Goat trotted over the bridge to the green hill. Middle Goat walked down to the bridge. He was careful and quick. Middle Goat's horns were still small. Middle Goat's hooves went trip-trap on the bridge. Troll: Who is trip-trapping over my bridge? Middle Goat: It is only me, the middle goat. Troll: I will eat you up! Middle Goat: Do not eat me, Troll. Middle Goat: Wait for my brother, Big Goat. Middle Goat: He is bigger than me. Troll: Bigger still? Troll: Then go, middle goat. Middle Goat trotted over the bridge to the green hill. The troll was still hungry. Two goats had crossed to the green hill. The troll had eaten nothing all day. Troll: No more goats will trick me. The troll waited under the dark bridge. He listened hard for more hooves. Big Goat was the biggest of the three. Troll: The next goat, I will eat. Big Goat walked down to the bridge. Big Goat's hooves went trip-trap on the bridge. Troll: Who is trip-trapping over my bridge? Big Goat: It is I, the big goat. Troll: I will eat you up! Big Goat: Come and try, Troll. Troll: You are not small like your brothers. Big Goat: No, I am big and strong. Troll: I will eat you now! The troll jumped onto the bridge. The troll was hungry and angry. The troll ran at Big Goat. Big Goat did not run. Big Goat lowered his sharp horns. He charged at the troll. Big Goat's horns hit the troll hard. The troll flew off the bridge. The troll fell into the water below. Troll: Help me, I am falling! The water carried the troll away. Big Goat stood alone on the bridge. Big Goat's legs were strong. Big Goat: The bridge is safe now. Big Goat trotted to the green hill. Little Goat: You crossed the bridge! Middle Goat: Is the troll gone? Big Goat: The troll fell in the water. Big Goat: He will not come back. Little Goat: We can eat all day now. The three goats ate the fresh grass. They grew fat on the green hill. Middle Goat: This grass is the best. Big Goat: We are safe and full. The three goats lived happily on the green hill.

note.en: Add -er to compare two things, -est for the most of all: big → bigger → biggest.

note.en: The name, a colon, then the exact words. Readers know who is speaking without pages of speech marks.

q.en: Why did the goats want to cross the bridge?

options: To eat the grass on the green hill

why.en: Their hill was bare and dry, and the hill across the bridge was green.
why.fa: تپهٔ آن‌ها خشک بود و تپهٔ آن‌طرف پل سبز.

q.en: Who crossed the bridge first?
q.fa: چه کسی اول از پل رد شد؟

why.en: Little Goat says 'I will go first' and walks down.
why.fa: بز کوچک می‌گوید «اول من می‌روم» و راه می‌افتد.

q.en: How did the small goats save themselves?
q.fa: بزهای کوچک چطور خودشان را نجات دادند؟

options: They sent the troll after a bigger brother.
They pushed the troll into the water.

why.en: Each one says a bigger brother is coming, so the troll waits for a better meal.
why.fa: هر کدام می‌گوید برادر بزرگ‌تری می‌آید، پس ترول منتظر شکار بهتری می‌ماند.

q.en: What did Big Goat do to the troll?
q.fa: بز بزرگ با ترول چه کرد؟

options: He charged it with his horns.
He gave it the fresh grass.
He ran away with his brothers.
He asked it to leave politely.

why.en: He lowered his horns, charged, and the troll flew off the bridge.
why.fa: شاخ‌هایش را پایین آورد، حمله کرد و ترول از پل پرت شد.

q.en: How does the story end?
q.fa: داستان چطور تمام می‌شود؟

options: The three goats eat and live happily.

why.en: They eat the fresh grass, grow fat and live happily on the green hill.
why.fa: علف تازه می‌خورند، چاق می‌شوند و خوشحال روی تپهٔ سبز زندگی می‌کنند.

q.en: The troll lived under the bridge.
q.fa: ترول زیر پل زندگی می‌کرد.

why.en: 'Under the bridge, a troll lived in the dark.'
why.fa: «زیر پل، ترولی در تاریکی زندگی می‌کرد.»

q.en: Middle Goat had large horns.
q.fa: بز وسطی شاخ‌های بزرگی داشت.

why.en: 'Middle Goat's horns were still small.'
why.fa: «شاخ‌های بز وسطی هنوز کوچک بود.»

q.en: The troll came back after the fight.
q.fa: ترول بعد از نبرد برگشت.

why.en: Big Goat says 'He will not come back', and the water carried him away.
why.fa: بز بزرگ می‌گوید «برنمی‌گردد» و آب او را با خود برد.

q.en: Was Big Goat brave or just strong?
q.fa: بز بزرگ شجاع بود یا فقط قوی؟

model.en: Both, and the story needs both. Strong horns mean nothing if he runs, and not running means nothing if the troll just walks over him. He stands still, warns nobody, and uses what he has.
model.fa: هر دو، و داستان به هر دو نیاز دارد. شاخ قوی اگر فرار کند بی‌فایده است و ایستادن هم اگر ترول از رویش رد شود بی‌فایده. او می‌ایستد و از آنچه دارد استفاده می‌کند.

tip.en: Choose one, then use two moments from the story.
tip.fa: یکی را انتخاب کن و دو لحظه از داستان را شاهد بیاور.

q.en: Why does the story have three goats and not one?
q.fa: چرا داستان سه بز دارد و نه یکی؟

model.en: The three sizes make the trick work twice and give the ending weight. The small ones show that words can save you; the big one shows that words are not always enough. One goat could not teach both.
model.fa: سه اندازه باعث می‌شود حقه دو بار جواب دهد و پایان وزن بگیرد. کوچک‌ترها نشان می‌دهند حرف می‌تواند نجاتت دهد و بزرگ نشان می‌دهد حرف همیشه کافی نیست. با یک بز هر دو درس ممکن نبود.

tip.en: Think about repetition and size, then answer in three sentences.
tip.fa: به تکرار و اندازه فکر کن و در سه جمله جواب بده.

blurb.en: A girl finds an empty house, three bowls of porridge and three beds. The bears find her.
blurb.fa: دختری خانه‌ای خالی، سه کاسه فرنی و سه تخت پیدا می‌کند. خرس‌ها او را پیدا می‌کنند.

pairs.en: Three bears lived in a house in a big wood.
pairs.fa: سه خرس در خانه‌ای در جنگل بزرگی زندگی می‌کردند.

pairs.en: One was a big bear, one was a middle bear.
pairs.fa: یکی خرس بزرگ بود، یکی خرس متوسط.

pairs.en: One was a little bear.
pairs.fa: یکی خرس کوچک بود.

pairs.en: Every morning, the bears made hot porridge.
pairs.fa: هر صبح خرس‌ها فرنی داغ درست می‌کردند.

pairs.en: But today, the porridge was too hot to eat.
pairs.fa: اما امروز فرنی برای خوردن خیلی داغ بود.

pairs.en: "Let's walk while it cools," said the big bear.
pairs.fa: خرس بزرگ گفت: «بیایید قدم بزنیم تا خنک شود.»

pairs.en: The three bears walked into the wood.
pairs.fa: سه خرس به جنگل رفتند.

pairs.en: Nearby, a girl named Goldilocks walked through the wood too.
pairs.fa: نزدیک آنجا دختری به نام گلدلاکس هم در جنگل قدم می‌زد.

pairs.en: She had golden hair, like her name.
pairs.fa: موهای طلایی داشت، مثل اسمش.

pairs.en: Goldilocks saw a small house among the trees.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس خانه‌ای کوچک میان درختان دید.

pairs.en: She walked toward it.
pairs.fa: به سمت آن رفت.

pairs.en: Goldilocks was hungry after her long walk.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس بعد از قدم طولانی گرسنه بود.

pairs.en: She knocked on the door, but no one answered.
pairs.fa: در زد، اما کسی جواب نداد.

pairs.en: She pushed the door open and walked inside.
pairs.fa: در را هل داد و داخل رفت.

pairs.en: Goldilocks saw three bowls of porridge on the table.
pairs.fa: سه کاسه فرنی روی میز دید.

pairs.en: She tasted the porridge in the big bowl.
pairs.fa: فرنی کاسهٔ بزرگ را چشید.

pairs.en: It burned her tongue.
pairs.fa: زبانش سوخت.

pairs.en: "This is too hot!" said Goldilocks.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس گفت: «این خیلی داغ است!»

pairs.en: Next, she tasted the porridge in the middle bowl.
pairs.fa: بعد فرنی کاسهٔ وسطی را چشید.

pairs.en: "This is too cold!" said Goldilocks.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس گفت: «این خیلی سرد است!»

pairs.en: Then she tasted the porridge in the little bowl.
pairs.fa: بعد فرنی کاسهٔ کوچک را چشید.

pairs.en: "This is just right!" said Goldilocks.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس گفت: «این دقیقاً درست است!»

pairs.en: Goldilocks ate up all the porridge in the little bowl.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس تمام فرنی کاسهٔ کوچک را خورد.

pairs.en: After she ate, Goldilocks saw three chairs by the fire.
pairs.fa: بعد از غذا، گلدلاکس سه صندلی کنار شومینه دید.

pairs.en: Then she climbed onto the big chair.
pairs.fa: بعد روی صندلی بزرگ نشست.

pairs.en: "This is too hard!" said Goldilocks.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس گفت: «این خیلی سفت است!»

pairs.en: Her back began to hurt.
pairs.fa: کمرش شروع به درد کرد.

pairs.en: She climbed onto the middle chair.
pairs.fa: روی صندلی وسطی نشست.

pairs.en: "This is too soft!" said Goldilocks.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس گفت: «این خیلی نرم است!»

pairs.en: She climbed onto the little chair.
pairs.fa: روی صندلی کوچک نشست.

pairs.en: "This is just right!" said Goldilocks.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس گفت: «این دقیقاً درست است!»

pairs.en: But the little chair was too small for her.
pairs.fa: اما صندلی کوچک برایش خیلی کوچک بود.

pairs.en: It broke into pieces under her weight.
pairs.fa: زیر وزنش تکه‌تکه شد.

pairs.en: Goldilocks fell down onto the floor.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس روی زمین افتاد.

pairs.en: She stood up and looked at the broken chair.
pairs.fa: بلند شد و به صندلی شکسته نگاه کرد.

pairs.en: Goldilocks was tired from her long walk.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس از قدم طولانی خسته بود.

pairs.en: No one else was in the house.
pairs.fa: کس دیگری در خانه نبود.

pairs.en: She walked upstairs to look for a bed.
pairs.fa: از پله‌ها بالا رفت تا تختی پیدا کند.

pairs.en: Goldilocks lay down on the big bed.
pairs.fa: روی تخت بزرگ دراز کشید.

pairs.en: "This is too hard!" said Goldilocks.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس گفت: «این خیلی سفت است!»

pairs.en: She lay down on the middle bed.
pairs.fa: روی تخت وسطی دراز کشید.

pairs.en: "This is too soft!" said Goldilocks.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس گفت: «این خیلی نرم است!»

pairs.en: She lay down on the little bed.
pairs.fa: روی تخت کوچک دراز کشید.

pairs.en: "This is just right!" said Goldilocks.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس گفت: «این دقیقاً درست است!»

pairs.en: Goldilocks pulled up the blanket and closed her eyes.
pairs.fa: گلدلاکس پتو را بالا کشید و چشم‌هایش را بست.

pairs.en: Soon, she fell fast asleep in the little bed.
pairs.fa: به‌زودی روی تخت کوچک خواب عمیقی کرد.

pairs.en: Soon, the three bears came home from their walk.
pairs.fa: به‌زودی سه خرس از قدم زدن برگشتند.

pairs.en: The door of their house was open.
pairs.fa: درِ خانه‌شان باز بود.

pairs.en: The hungry bears saw their empty bowls.
pairs.fa: خرس‌های گرسنه کاسه‌های خالی را دیدند.

pairs.en: "Someone ate my porridge!" said the big bear.
pairs.fa: خرس بزرگ گفت: «کسی فرنی من را خورد!»

pairs.en: "Someone ate my porridge too!" said the middle bear.
pairs.fa: خرس وسطی گفت: «کسی فرنی من را هم خورد!»

pairs.en: "Someone ate all my porridge!" cried the little bear.
pairs.fa: خرس کوچک گریه کرد: «کسی تمام فرنی من را خورد!»

pairs.en: Then they saw their chairs by the fire.

stories.text: Three bears lived in a house in a big wood. One was a big bear, one was a middle bear. One was a little bear. Every morning, the bears made hot porridge. But today, the porridge was too hot to eat. "Let's walk while it cools," said the big bear. The three bears walked into the wood. Nearby, a girl named Goldilocks walked through the wood too. She had golden hair, like her name. Goldilocks saw a small house among the trees. She walked toward it. Goldilocks was hungry after her long walk. She knocked on the door, but no one answered. She pushed the door open and walked inside. Goldilocks saw three bowls of porridge on the table. She tasted the porridge in the big bowl. It burned her tongue. "This is too hot!" said Goldilocks. Next, she tasted the porridge in the middle bowl. "This is too cold!" said Goldilocks. Then she tasted the porridge in the little bowl. "This is just right!" said Goldilocks. Goldilocks ate up all the porridge in the little bowl. After she ate, Goldilocks saw three chairs by the fire. Then she climbed onto the big chair. "This is too hard!" said Goldilocks. Her back began to hurt. She climbed onto the middle chair. "This is too soft!" said Goldilocks. She climbed onto the little chair. "This is just right!" said Goldilocks. But the little chair was too small for her. It broke into pieces under her weight. Goldilocks fell down onto the floor. She stood up and looked at the broken chair. Goldilocks was tired from her long walk. No one else was in the house. She walked upstairs to look for a bed. Goldilocks lay down on the big bed. "This is too hard!" said Goldilocks. She lay down on the middle bed. "This is too soft!" said Goldilocks. She lay down on the little bed. "This is just right!" said Goldilocks. Goldilocks pulled up the blanket and closed her eyes. Soon, she fell fast asleep in the little bed. Soon, the three bears came home from their walk. The door of their house was open. The hungry bears saw their empty bowls. "Someone ate my porridge!" said the big bear. "Someone ate my porridge too!" said the middle bear. "Someone ate all my porridge!" cried the little bear. Then they saw their chairs by the fire. "Someone sat in my chair!" said the big bear. "Someone sat in my chair too!" said the middle bear. The little bear looked at the pieces on the floor. "Someone broke my chair!" he cried. They did not know who came, so they walked upstairs. Upstairs, the three bears looked at their beds. "Someone slept in my bed!" said the big bear. "Someone slept in my bed too!" said the middle bear. "Someone slept in my bed!" cried the little bear. Goldilocks was still asleep in the little bear's bed. The little bear cried, and Goldilocks woke up. She opened her eyes and saw the three bears. Goldilocks jumped up, scared of the bears. Her heart beat fast. She ran out of the bed and down the stairs. Goldilocks ran out the door and into the wood. She never came back to the small house again.

note.en: 'Too hot to eat' means so hot that it cannot be eaten. 'Too' is always negative in this pattern.

q.en: Was Goldilocks right to go into the house?
q.fa: گلدلاکس حق داشت وارد خانه شود؟

model.en: No: knocking and getting no answer is not permission. She then ate the food, broke a chair and slept in a bed, and the story lets her pay for it with fright rather than a lesson in manners. Being hungry explains it; it does not make it right.
model.fa: نه: در زدن و جواب نگرفتن اجازه نیست. بعد غذا خورد، صندلی شکست و در تختی خوابید، و داستان به جای درس ادب، با ترس جریمه‌اش می‌کند. گرسنگی توضیح می‌دهد اما توجیه نمی‌کند.

tip.en: Give your verdict first, then the two actions that decide it.
tip.fa: اول حکمت را بگو، بعد دو کاری که آن را تعیین می‌کند.

q.en: Why does the story repeat 'too hard, too soft, just right'?
q.fa: چرا داستان «خیلی سفت، خیلی نرم، دقیقاً درست» را تکرار می‌کند؟

model.en: The repetition is the lesson. Three tries with the same words teach 'too' and 'just right' without explaining them, and a learner can guess the third line before reading it. That is also why children ask for the same story again.
model.fa: تکرار همان درس است. سه تلاش با همان کلمه‌ها «too» و «just right» را بدون توضیح یاد می‌دهند و زبان‌آموز می‌تواند جملهٔ سوم را قبل از خواندن حدس بزند. به همین دلیل بچه‌ها یک داستان را دوباره می‌خواهند.

pairs.en: The wolf saw the flowers.

pairs.fa: گفت: «چرا برایش گل نمی‌چینی؟»

stories.text: Little Red Riding Hood lived in a small village. Her grandmother lived across the woods. Grandmother gave her a red hood to wear. She wore the red hood. The village called her Little Red Riding Hood. One day, Grandmother was sick. Her mother filled a basket with food. She put cake and bread into the basket. "Take this to Grandmother," said her mother. "Do not leave the path," her mother called. "I will be safe," said Little Red Riding Hood. Then she took the basket and went into the woods. Little Red Riding Hood walked down the path. A wolf came out of the woods. "Good day," said the wolf with a smile. "Why do you have that basket?" he called. "This food is for my sick grandmother," she said. Grandmother lived across the woods. The wolf saw the flowers. "Why not pick flowers for her?" he said. Little Red Riding Hood left the path to pick flowers. The wolf ran through the woods. The wolf reached the small house. He knocked on the door two times. "Who is there?" called Grandmother from her bed. "It is me, Little Red Riding Hood," said the wolf. "Come in, the door is open," said Grandmother. The wolf opened the door and went inside. The wolf swallowed Grandmother in one bite. He wore Grandmother's cap. He climbed into Grandmother's bed to hide. He pulled the blanket up to hide. Then the wolf waited for Little Red Riding Hood. Soon Little Red Riding Hood reached the quiet house. She knocked gently on the wooden door two times. "Come in, the door is open," said the wolf. Little Red Riding Hood walked slowly through the door. She saw her grandmother under the blanket. But her grandmother's face looked strange today. "Grandmother, what big eyes you have!" she said. "All the better to see you with," said the wolf. "Grandmother, what big ears you have!" she said. "All the better to hear you with," said the wolf. "Grandmother, what big teeth you have!" she said. "All the better to eat you with!" said the wolf. The wolf jumped up and swallowed Little Red Riding Hood. The wolf's stomach was full, and he fell asleep. A huntsman walked past the small house. He heard snores from inside the house. The huntsman thought Grandmother lived in that house. He knocked, but no one came to the door. The huntsman opened the door and looked inside. He saw the wolf asleep in Grandmother's bed. The wolf's stomach looked big. The huntsman thought Grandmother might be inside. He took out a knife and cut open the wolf. Little Red Riding Hood jumped out safe! Then Grandmother climbed out of the wolf too. She was safe. Little Red Riding Hood hugged her grandmother. The huntsman found heavy stones. Grandmother and Little Red Riding Hood filled the wolf. They put the heavy stones inside him. Soon the wolf woke up. He wanted to run from the house. But the stones were too heavy to carry. The wolf fell down and died in the woods. Little Red Riding Hood was safe. The huntsman smiled. They all went inside Grandmother's small house. Little Red Riding Hood gave her the basket. Grandmother ate the cake and the bread. "Thank you," said Grandmother to the huntsman. "It was my pleasure," said the huntsman. The huntsman left. "I will never leave the path," she said. "That is a good lesson," said Grandmother. Little Red Riding Hood smiled and kissed her grandmother. From that day on, she never left the path.

stories.text: A miller died and left his three sons his mill, his donkey, and his cat. The youngest son got the cat and thought it was a poor gift. "Give me a pair of boots," said the cat, "and I will make you rich." The cat put on the boots, filled a bag with carrots, and caught rabbits in a field. He took the rabbits to the king and said they were a present from the Marquis of Carabas. The king was pleased, and the presents kept coming. One day the cat told his master to swim in the river when the king's coach passed. The cat shouted that the Marquis was drowning and that thieves had taken his clothes. The king gave him fine clothes, and the princess fell in love with him. The cat ran ahead and told the farmers to say the fields belonged to the Marquis. When the king asked, they all said yes, so the Marquis seemed very rich. The cat came to a castle owned by an ogre who could change into any animal. "Can you become a lion?" asked the cat, and the ogre became a lion. "Can you become something very small, like a mouse?" The ogre became a mouse, and the cat ate him in one bite. The Marquis married the princess, and the cat became a great lord.

blurb.en: A brother and sister fly to Barcelona, and one wrong bus turns lunch into a day nobody planned.
blurb.fa: برادر و خواهری به بارسلونا پرواز می‌کنند و یک اتوبوس اشتباه، ناهار را به روزی تبدیل می‌کند که هیچ‌کس نقشه‌اش را نکشیده بود.

summary.en: Daniel and Julia are brother and sister, and they are both university students in London, where they share a house. Their parents are Arthur and Sarah, and both of them speak Spanish. The two of them are packing for Barcelona, where they will spend a term as exchange students. Their father comes into Daniel's room with a pile of money that he and their mother have saved for the trip, and their mother drives them to the airport. Julia is nervous in the car, but the airport calms her down, and the two of them board the plane.
summary.fa: دانیل و جولیا خواهر و برادرند و هر دو در لندن دانشجو هستند و خانه‌ای را با هم شریک‌اند. پدر و مادرشان آرتور و سارا هستند و هر دو اسپانیایی حرف می‌زنند. آن دو برای بارسلونا بار می‌بندند تا یک ترم به‌عنوان دانشجوی تبادلی آنجا باشند. پدرشان با پولی که خودش و مادر پس‌انداز کرده‌اند به اتاق دانیل می‌آید و مادرشان آن دو را به فرودگاه می‌برد. جولیا در ماشین مضطرب است، اما فرودگاه آرامش می‌کند و هر دو سوار هواپیما می‌شوند.

summary.en: They land in Barcelona, where Daniel's friend Armando is waiting. He hugs Daniel and kisses Julia on both cheeks; Julia is shy, so she goes quiet and her face turns red. A taxi takes the three of them to Armando's flat, which will be home for the term. At lunchtime Armando suggests two restaurants: a paella place called La Paella Loca, and a fish restaurant next door. Julia does not want a crowded bus, so they split up, and Daniel falls asleep on his bus. He wakes up in Valencia. His phone battery is dead and his sister's number is only in the phone, so he cannot call her. He eats paella alone, is embarrassed by how strange the day is, then phones his parents in London and asks them to tell Julia where he is. He pays for a hotel room in cash and sleeps.
summary.fa: در بارسلونا فرود می‌آیند و آرماندو، دوست دانیل، آنجاست. دانیل را در آغوش می‌گیرد و جولیا را بر دو گونه می‌بوسد؛ جولیا خجالتی است، ساکت می‌شود و صورتش سرخ. تاکسی هر سه را به آپارتمان آرماندو می‌برد که خانهٔ آن ترم خواهد بود. وقت ناهار آرماندو دو رستوران پیشنهاد می‌دهد: پائیا فروشی به نام لا پائیا لوکا و رستوران ماهی که کنار آن است. جولیا اتوبوس شلوغ نمی‌خواهد، پس جدا می‌شوند و دانیل در اتوبوس خوابش می‌برد. در والنسیا بیدار می‌شود. باتری گوشی‌اش تمام شده و شمارهٔ خواهرش فقط در گوشی است، پس نمی‌تواند زنگ بزند. تنها پائیا می‌خورد، از عجیب بودن روز خجالت‌زده می‌شود، بعد به پدر و مادرش در لندن زنگ می‌زند و می‌خواهد به جولیا بگویند کجاست. پول اتاق هتل را نقد می‌دهد و می‌خوابد.

summary.en: In the morning Daniel eats in his hotel room and works out that he has very little money left. Outside he sees a lorry with a picture of paella on the side: it belongs to La Paella Loca and brings rice to Barcelona every week. He persuades the driver to take him back, and rides between the rice boxes in the dark. Something moves: an old man is hiding there. The driver stops to warn Daniel to be quiet, and the old man stays hidden. He then tells Daniel why he is travelling: years ago he left for a job in the United States and lost touch with the woman he loved and the son he has never met, and he has just found out that the son, whose name is Armando, lives in Barcelona near the restaurant.
summary.fa: صبح دانیل در اتاق هتل غذا می‌خورد و می‌فهمد پول کمی برایش مانده. بیرون کامیونی با تصویر پائیا می‌بیند: مال لا پائیا لوکاست و هر هفته برنج به بارسلونا می‌برد. راننده را راضی می‌کند او را برگرداند و در تاریکی میان جعبه‌های برنج می‌نشیند. چیزی حرکت می‌کند: پیرمردی آنجا پنهان شده. راننده می‌ایستد تا به دانیل هشدار دهد ساکت باشد و پیرمرد پنهان می‌ماند. بعد برای دانیل می‌گوید چرا سفر می‌کند: سال‌ها پیش برای کاری به آمریکا رفت و ارتباطش را با زنی که دوستش داشت و پسری که هرگز ندیده از دست داد، و تازه فهمیده پسر، که نامش آرماندو است، در بارسلونا نزدیک همان رستوران زندگی می‌کند.

meaning.en: a student who studies for a time in another country

vocab.example: They will spend a term in Barcelona as exchange students.
vocab.exampleFa: آن دو یک ترم به‌عنوان دانشجوی تبادلی در بارسلونا خواهند بود.

meaning.en: worried and not calm

vocab.example: Julia is nervous in the car on the way to the airport.
vocab.exampleFa: جولیا در ماشین تا فرودگاه مضطرب است.

meaning.en: a set of rooms to live in, part of a larger building

vocab.example: A taxi takes them to Armando's flat.
vocab.exampleFa: تاکسی آن‌ها را به آپارتمان آرماندو می‌برد.

meaning.en: a car you pay to ride in

vocab.example: The taxi costs forty-one euros.
vocab.exampleFa: کرایهٔ تاکسی چهل‌و‌یک یورو است.

meaning.en: a Spanish rice dish with meat or seafood

vocab.example: He eats paella alone in Valencia.
vocab.exampleFa: او در والنسیا تنها پائیا می‌خورد.

meaning.en: the part of a phone that holds power

vocab.example: His phone battery is dead, so he cannot call.
vocab.exampleFa: باتری گوشی‌اش تمام شده، پس نمی‌تواند زنگ بزند.

meaning.en: feeling foolish in front of people

vocab.example: He is embarrassed by how strange the day is.
vocab.exampleFa: از عجیب بودن روز خجالت‌زده است.

meaning.en: a male child

vocab.example: The old man has never met his son.
vocab.exampleFa: پیرمرد هرگز پسرش را ندیده است.

meaning.en: go towards a place

expressions.example: They head for the airport in their mother's car.
expressions.exampleFa: با ماشین مادرشان به سمت فرودگاه می‌روند.

meaning.en: tell the airport desk you have arrived

expressions.example: At the airport they check in for the flight.
expressions.exampleFa: در فرودگاه کارهای پرواز را انجام می‌دهند.

meaning.en: more than a person can deal with

expressions.example: He starts laughing because it's all too much.
expressions.exampleFa: شروع می‌کند به خندیدن چون دیگر بیش از حد تحملش است.

meaning.en: you finally understand what has really happened

expressions.example: After dinner, reality sinks in: he is in the wrong city.
expressions.exampleFa: بعد از شام واقعیت جا می‌افتد: او در شهر اشتباهی است.

grammar.example: We are leaving for Spain today.

note.en: A fixed arrangement uses the present continuous, not 'will': the ticket is bought, so it is happening.
note.fa: برای برنامهٔ قطعی از حال استمراری استفاده می‌شود، نه will: بلیت خریده شده، پس انجام می‌شود.

grammar.example: He got on the bus, fell asleep and woke up in Valencia.

note.en: The story moves forward with past simple verbs, one action after another.
note.fa: داستان با فعل‌های گذشتهٔ ساده جلو می‌رود، کاری پس از کار دیگر.

grammar.example: I have never met my son.

note.en: 'Have/has never + past participle' covers all of life up to now, which is why it fits a man explaining his whole history.
note.fa: «have/has never + قسمت سوم فعل» تمام زندگی تا امروز را در بر می‌گیرد و به همین دلیل برای کسی که کل گذشته‌اش را توضیح می‌دهد مناسب است.

grammar.example: He cannot call because his battery is dead.

note.en: 'Because' gives the reason for the sentence before it; the reason comes after.
note.fa: «because» دلیل جملهٔ قبل را می‌آورد و دلیل بعد از آن می‌آید.

q.en: Where do Daniel and Julia study?
q.fa: دانیل و جولیا کجا درس می‌خوانند؟

why.en: They are students in London and go to Barcelona only for a term.
why.fa: آن‌ها در لندن دانشجو هستند و فقط یک ترم به بارسلونا می‌روند.

q.en: What do their parents give them for the trip?
q.fa: پدر و مادر برای سفر چه به آن‌ها می‌دهند؟

why.en: Their father brings a pile of money saved for the trip.
why.fa: پدرشان پولی را که برای سفر پس‌انداز شده می‌آورد.

q.en: Why does Daniel end up in Valencia?
q.fa: چرا دانیل سر از والنسیا درمی‌آورد؟

options: He takes an express bus by mistake
He misses his stop on purpose
The taxi driver takes him there
He wants to see the city

why.en: He sleeps on the bus and wakes at the end of the express route.
why.fa: در اتوبوس می‌خوابد و در پایان مسیر سریع بیدار می‌شود.

q.en: Why can he not telephone his sister?
q.fa: چرا نمی‌تواند به خواهرش زنگ بزند؟

options: He has no money for a call
He is too shy to call
The battery is dead and her number is in the phone

why.en: The number is stored only in the phone, and the phone will not turn on.
why.fa: شماره فقط در گوشی ذخیره است و گوشی روشن نمی‌شود.

q.en: Who is the old man in the lorry?
q.fa: پیرمرد داخل کامیون کیست؟

why.en: He is looking for a son called Armando who lives in Barcelona, and Armando is Daniel's friend.
why.fa: دنبال پسری به نام آرماندو در بارسلونا می‌گردد و آرماندو دوست دانیل است.

q.en: Julia talks easily to new people.
q.fa: جولیا راحت با آدم‌های تازه حرف می‌زند.

why.en: She is shy, goes quiet and her face turns red.
why.fa: خجالتی است، ساکت می‌شود و صورتش سرخ می‌شود.

q.en: Armando is a teacher.
q.fa: آرماندو معلم است.

why.en: He cannot come to lunch because he has a class.
why.fa: نمی‌تواند برای ناهار بیاید چون کلاس دارد.

q.en: Daniel pays for the hotel with a credit card.
q.fa: دانیل هزینهٔ هتل را با کارت اعتباری می‌دهد.

why.en: He has no credit cards and pays in cash.
why.fa: کارت اعتباری ندارد و نقد می‌پردازد.

blanks.sentence: Julia is ___ in the car on the way to the airport.
Daniel sleeps on the ___ and wakes up in Valencia.

hint.en: The vehicle he takes to the paella restaurant.
hint.fa: وسیله‌ای که با آن به رستوران پائیا می‌رود.

blanks.sentence: The old man is looking for his ___.

hint.en: The child he has never met.

q.en: Whose mistake causes the worst part of the day?
q.fa: اشتباه چه کسی بدترین بخش روز را می‌سازد؟

model.en: Mostly Daniel's, but not only his. He got on a bus without checking where it went and fell asleep, which is his mistake. Julia's refusal to take a crowded bus split them up, and the driver's assumption that a passenger knows the route did the rest. The story is funny because no single person is to blame.
model.fa: بیشتر اشتباه دانیل است، اما نه فقط او. بدون اینکه ببیند اتوبوس کجا می‌رود سوار شد و خوابید، و این اشتباه او بود. امتناع جولیا از اتوبوس شلوغ آن‌ها را جدا کرد و فرض راننده که مسافر مسیر را می‌داند بقیهٔ کار را کرد. داستان خنده‌دار است چون هیچ‌کس تنها مقصر نیست.

tip.en: Name the person, then one decision from each of them.
tip.fa: نام شخص را بگو، بعد از هر کدام یک تصمیم بیاور.

q.en: Why is the meeting in the lorry the story's turning point?
q.fa: چرا دیدار در کامیون نقطهٔ چرخش داستان است؟

model.en: Because it turns a comic accident into a human story. Up to that point the day is only an inconvenience; the old man's search gives it weight, and the coincidence that his son is Daniel's friend means the two plots have been the same plot all along.
model.fa: چون حادثه‌ای خنده‌دار را به داستانی انسانی تبدیل می‌کند. تا آن لحظه روز فقط یک دردسر است؛ جست‌وجوی پیرمرد به آن وزن می‌دهد و این تصادف که پسرش دوست دانیل است نشان می‌دهد دو خط داستان از اول یکی بوده‌اند.

tip.en: Say what changes for the reader, then point at the coincidence.
tip.fa: بگو برای خواننده چه عوض می‌شود، بعد به آن تصادف اشاره کن.

book.title: Short Stories in English for Beginners
book.author: Olly Richards

note.en: A companion, not a copy. Read chapters 1-3 in your own copy of the book; this page gives summary, vocabulary, grammar and questions to work through afterwards. No chapter text is reproduced here.
note.fa: این صفحه همراهِ کتاب است، نه رونوشت آن. فصل‌های ۱ تا ۳ را در نسخهٔ خودتان بخوانید؛ اینجا خلاصه، واژگان، گرامر و پرسش می‌آید تا بعد از خواندن کار کنید. متنی از فصل‌ها بازتولید نشده است.
